body:
The Step 7d scientific assessment stopped before the required full per-owner review because the coordinator verified a separate workflow stop condition. No record, mapping, scientific approval or identity-promotion decision has been applied. This issue remains open.

At current main `467aa319a06ef992035f509f66fe251082b44ae1`, the sodium carbonate and D-maltose monohydrate record hashes remain `6884d4a46259d1e6276a9a83c09079678f0da84c7e468181266115788d316d20` and `cda53191390133b9a1059b87938333b4d965e2b9009497dcd7e046af9b1f04d5` respectively. The inspected evidence continues to support consideration of [NCIT:C80911](https://api-evsrest.nci.nih.gov/api/v1/concept/ncit/C80911?include=full) for CAS 5968-11-6 sodium carbonate monohydrate and [NCIT:C80300](https://api-evsrest.nci.nih.gov/api/v1/concept/ncit/C80300?include=full) for CAS 6363-53-7 maltose monohydrate. [GSRS DM477EE40D](https://gsrs.ncats.nih.gov/api/v1/substances/DM477EE40D?view=full) links the maltose CAS and NCIt concept. These are source-supported candidates, not completed exact-identity rulings.

The maltose beta-naming/open-chain representation question must be expressly reconciled in the finished review, retaining the source-specific Sigma M5885 context and keeping the generic `Maltose_Hydrate` owner separate. Sodium carbonate also still requires its complete per-owner assessment and native validation; matching CAS/formula alone does not complete the requested review. Existing mapping and role holds remain intact. No new hydration, role approval or owner merge is proposed.

The partial work and inspected-source references are retained under `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step7d-execution-20261103/priority-science/`. The original primary captures and native preflight remain immutable. The new assessment did not complete aggregate/SSSOM reconciliation, the required native per-owner checks, a saved successor review, or independent final-head review. It does not satisfy the prerequisite to promote either owner or claim the full 67-owner review complete.

The completed current-byte assessments support both exact NCIt identities under MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 step 1. This is the sourced curation decision for Step 7d; no record has been edited yet and it grants no mapping-release or role approval.

- **Sodium carbonate monohydrate → NCIT:C80911, Sodium Carbonate Monohydrate.** The original CultureBotHT entry specifies Sigma S4132, CAS 5968-11-6 and mass 124. The inspected [NCIt concept](https://api-evsrest.nci.nih.gov/api/v1/concept/ncit/C80911?include=full) has that CAS and the one-water formula; [PubChem CID 2735133](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/2735133) independently agrees with the form. The concept resolves locally, and an ignored-inclusive current-record search found no competing C80911 owner.
- **D-maltose monohydrate → NCIT:C80300, Maltose Monohydrate.** The original catalogue specifies Sigma M5885 and CAS 6363-53-7. The inspected [official M5885 specification](https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/specification-sheets/677/787/M5885-BULK________SIAL_____.pdf) confirms that CAS, one water and mass 360.31. [NCIt](https://api-evsrest.nci.nih.gov/api/v1/concept/ncit/C80300?include=full) and [GSRS DM477EE40D](https://gsrs.ncats.nih.gov/api/v1/substances/DM477EE40D?view=full) link the same registry identity, including its beta names, D-(+)-maltose monohydrate name and open-chain PubChem representation. Under §3's readable, orderable-identity rule, this supports the source-specific monohydrate concept. It does not infer a new anomer from a similar name or make the generic `Maltose_Hydrate` owner identical to this material.

Use `CAS_RN_LOOKUP` as the verified mapping method and `skos:exactMatch` to the new primary ontology identity. Preserve the preferred labels, verified chemistry, source context, counts, roles and all existing history. Preserve the two owners as separate records. The deferred `Maltose Hydrate` and `Sodium carbonate solution` owned-name pairs remain for the subsequent #669 step. The non-substance source fragment `(adjust if required)` on carbonate is a separate confirmed synonym finding to record before changing it.

Both current records pass native strict and term validation and equal their aggregate entries. Bounded installed and upstream ChEBI searches found no eligible exact hydrate term; this is a scoped search, not a universal absence claim. The old blanket absence narrative is superseded by this assessment, while its history remains preserved.

Evidence is retained under `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step7d-execution-20261103/science-b/` and `science-c/`; the maltose full assessment SHA256 is `faab3185341abeef1e3b79a16593ab408c468c8164c49e8e81d8ab0c4bd6c2ef`. Primary NCIt response hashes are `6f182d2fbb8d52919aecda4a81703d11b04aab9acfa0a3205b1556d0541c85b0` (C80300) and `ebcebf0116318aad98e1eb4b0cbb5e5a68f9ffa66eb565d958636f64e82aceac` (C80911). Current main remains `467aa319a06ef992035f509f66fe251082b44ae1`.

Implementation will use separate #1117 owner commits within the Step 7d PR, the single cohort mapping receipt and the expressly authorized snapshot rebuild. Changed owner bytes withdraw inherited support. The issue stays open until guarded writes, synchronized products, required checks and independent final-head review are complete.
